title: event-stream 3.3.6 and flatmap-stream 0.1.1
summary: A new maintainer took over event-stream and published 3.3.6 with a dependency on flatmap-stream 0.1.1, whose payload targeted Copay wallet builds and stayed installable for more than 78 days before any advisory existed. Package and advisory timestamps come from the npm registry and the GitHub Advisory Database listed in sources; the seven services, their descriptions and their lockfile resolution times are invented demo fixtures and name no real victim.

compromisedVersions.name: event-stream
compromisedVersions.note: Publish time from the event-stream packument time map. No install hook: the payload ran when flatmap-stream was required, which is why an install script scanner would have seen nothing.

compromisedVersions.name: flatmap-stream
compromisedVersions.note: Publish time is derived, not measured. npm removed 0.1.1 and the flatmap-stream packument keeps no time entry for it, so this uses the publish instant of event-stream 3.3.6, the version that first depended on it, as the earliest instant any build could install it. The npm postmortem states the dependency was added on 9 September 2018 in version 3.3.6.

advisories.summary: Embedded malicious code in event-stream: version 3.3.6 added a dependency on flatmap-stream, which carried code targeting Copay wallet builds.
Embedded malicious code in flatmap-stream 0.1.1. Published nearly two years after the event-stream advisory, which is itself a known-time fact worth replaying.

services.name: jobs-runner
services.description: Background job worker that watches child process trees, so it carries nodemon and ps-tree into production.

services.name: build-agent
services.description: Shared build machine that runs the gulp task graph for every frontend in the org.

services.name: asset-pipeline
services.description: Image and bundle pipeline whose lockfile was last refreshed the day before the compromise was noticed in public.

services.name: search-indexer
services.description: Batch indexer that forks worker processes and reaps their trees on shutdown.

services.name: checkout-web
services.description: Storefront checkout, frozen on an older lockfile since August and therefore never exposed.

services.name: ledger-api
services.description: Ledger service whose dependencies were refreshed two days after disclosure, landing on the fixed 4.x line.

services.name: notification-worker
services.description: Outbound email and push worker, refreshed the morning after the advisory and so on the pinned ps-tree fix.
